mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the Federal Funds rate above 5.25% for two consecutive months reduces near-term discounting of corporate cash flows, leading to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: FEDFUNDS crosses above 5.25% and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically different from zero during the trigger period (p > 0.05), or FEDFUNDS reverts below 5.25% within one month.

mechanism_narrative: Rising unemployment (UNRATE) below 4.5% for three consecutive months coincides with increased consumer caution, depressing short-term equity valuations and producing negative S&P 500 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE falls below 4.5% for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are positive in >70% of similar labor softening episodes (rolling IC > 0.2), or UNRATE reverts above 4.5% within two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sharp increase in industrial production (INDPRO) above its 12-month moving average signals accelerating economic demand, which elevates equity risk premia and drives positive S&P 500 5-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO crosses above 12-month moving average by 2% or more
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically significant (p > 0.10) during the signal, or INDPRO does not sustain the move above MA for 3 consecutive months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in consumer inflation-adjusted orders (HOUST) for four consecutive months indicates weakening demand, which compresses earnings growth forecasts and yields negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: HOUST falls for four consecutive months below its 12-month average
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >50% of prior order-weak episodes (rolling IC > 0.15), or HOUST recovers above MA within two months.

mechanism_narrative: When the monthly CPIAUCSL prints above 218 for two consecutive months, it suggests persistent inflation pressure, prompting the Fed to hold rates steady and increasing equity volatility that depresses 60-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: CPIAUCSL crosses above 218 and remains above for two consecutive months
failure_condition: 60-day forward returns are not negatively correlated with CPIAUCSL spikes (Pearson > 0.1), or CPIAUCSL reverts below 218 within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A sudden drop in labor market participation (PAYEMS) below 65 million for three months coincides with reduced consumer spending power, generating a negative 20-day S&P 500 forward return.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS falls below 65 million for three consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are positive in >60% of prior contraction episodes (rolling IC < 0.1), or PAYEMS recovers above 65M within two months.

mechanism_narrative: Consecutive months of rising retail sales (not directly observable in the provided proxies; this sketch is omitted as proxies are limited to the given list) — instead, use GDPC1 as a proxy for demand. A 10% rise in GDPC1 over two months predicts positive 5-day S&P 500 forward returns via optimism about future growth.
Note: Since direct demand proxies are limited to GDPC1, this sketch uses it as a demand proxy. (For completeness in format only.)
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 increases by 10% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 5-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.1) during the signal, or GDPC1 decline follows within one month.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous decline in both the unemployment rate (UNRATE) and industrial production (INDPRO) by at least 1 percentage point and 2% respectively over two months creates a contrarian signal that drives positive S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE decreases by ≥1pp AND INDPRO decreases by ≥2% over two consecutive months
failure_condition: 20-day forward returns are not statistically positive (p > 0.05) during such dual weakness, or either proxy recovers before the next trigger.
